value.rationale: Counting the number of singleton clusters and size of a uniformly tagged cluster is a canonical dependence question in set-partition probability. The exact opposite covariance signs between uniform-Bell mixing and two distinct natural extremal fixed-block laws show how conditioning on cluster richness reverses association; the second extremal stratum is the first one with nonconstant singleton count. The unrestricted all-n conditional covariance identity makes the contrast structural, not a one-off small-n numerical coincidence. The result does not assert a complete interior-k classification.
